fields.title: 3. Triggers — Expected vs Actual, Revised Expected Method
fields.md:
| Trigger | Previous issue's expectation | Actual (10/26) | Verdict | Revised expected method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T5 $40 billion 8-K | 2026-10-26 ~ 11-06 (price finalized 'next week' + 4 business days for 8-K) | No 8-K. CEO's closing announcement (10/25) came first | **Wrong** — not the date, but the premise that 'an 8-K will necessarily appear' was wrong. An off-balance-sheet SPV may not be subject to Item 2.03 | Checkpoint **2026-10-31** (after the 10/29–30 deadline passes) ~ 11/06. If there is no 8-K by 11/06, switch to the 'not subject to 8-K' hypothesis and verify via **10-K off-balance-sheet notes and IR materials**. Three paths specified in the verification method field |

(Source: `state.triggers_next_12m` previous value · Section 1 above)

**One-line lesson**: When writing a trigger as "if filing X appears," first state **whether that filing is legally required**. An off-balance-sheet structure changes the disclosure obligation itself — it was a design in which the trigger would never fire even if the event occurred.
